apiKeyModal.description: SailTrim uses your own Gemini key. It's free (1,500 queries per day, no cost) and never leaves your browser: it's stored only on your device and sent exclusively to Google.
apiKeyModal.noKeyBanner: 🧭 Don't have a key? Get it in 5 steps
apiKeyModal.placeholder: Paste your API key here (starts with AIza… or AQ.…)
apiKeyModal.fullGuide: View full guide: how to get your free key

apiGuide.title: How to get your free key
apiGuide.subtitle: It's a 5-minute process you only do once. Follow these steps:

steps.title: Open Google AI Studio
steps.text: Click the blue button below. A Google page will open in another browser tab.

steps.title: Sign in with your Google account
steps.text: Use whichever Gmail you want. It's free: Google won't ask you to pay at any point.

steps.title: Create your key
steps.text: Click the «Create API key» button. Google will generate your key automatically.

steps.title: Copy it
steps.text: Click the copy icon next to the key. It doesn't matter if it starts with «AIza» or «AQ.» — both are valid.

steps.title: Paste it in SailTrim
steps.text: Close this help, go back to the «Set up key» box, paste your key and press «Save». You're now ready to analyze trim!

apiGuide.watchVideo: Prefer to watch a video? Watch tutorial
apiGuide.disclaimer: With your key, Google gives you 1,500 free queries per day. SailTrim only uses it inside your browser: we never send it to any of our own servers.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: SailTrim runs entirely in your browser: no backend, no accounts, no analytics.

sections.title: What is stored and where
sections.text: Your boat profile, conversations, language and data mode are saved in this browser's local storage. They never leave your device.

sections.title: Your Gemini key
sections.text: The key is stored only in this browser and sent straight to Google when you query. SailTrim never receives it or forwards it to any server of its own.

sections.title: What is sent to Google
sections.text: Sailing conditions, your boat profile, chat messages and any images you attach travel to the Gemini API to generate the answer. From that point on, Google's handling applies.

sections.title: No tracking
sections.text: No analytics cookies, no advertising, no user profiles. The hosting provider may log basic technical data, such as IP address and date, when serving the page.

sections.title: How to delete it
sections.text: Remove the key from «Change key» and conversations from the history. Clearing the site data in your browser wipes everything, key included.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: SailTrim is an open source educational project. Use it at your own risk.

sections.title: No warranty
sections.text: The application is provided as is, with no guarantee of availability or accuracy. It may change or stop working without notice.

sections.title: Your key, your usage
sections.text: You use your own Gemini key and its quota and terms are Google's. SailTrim charges nothing and is not responsible for that usage.

sections.title: Safety on board
sections.text: Trim recommendations are advisory and do not replace the skipper's judgement, the rules of the sea or the manufacturer's instructions. The safety of the vessel and her crew is the responsibility of whoever is in command.

sections.title: AI-generated content
sections.text: Answers are produced by a language model and may contain errors. Check any manoeuvre or adjustment before carrying it out.

sections.title: Open source
sections.text: The code is distributed under the licence published in the GitHub repository.

rig.sloop: One mast and a mainsail: the most common rig and the easiest to trim.
rig.ketch: Two masts, the aft one shorter: spreads the sail and eases the helm.
rig.yawl: Two masts with a small one aft of the rudder: almost a sloop with a mizzen.
rig.cutter: One mast with two or three headsails: versatile in strong wind.
rig.catamaran: Two hulls and a lot of beam: no heel, but it needs its own sheet work.
rig.schooner: Two or more masts, the aft one equal or taller: classic reaching and running sail.
rig.other: Describe it below and I will take it into account.

materials.fiberglass: Polyester or epoxy: the usual choice, stiff and easy to repair.
materials.aluminum: Light and tough, shrugs off knocks and corrosion; common on long-distance boats.
materials.steel: Very strong but heavy: you lose some speed and gain toughness.
materials.wood: Classic and heavy; the hull works more and asks for upkeep.
materials.carbon: The lightest and stiffest: responds to fine tuning, but costs.
materials.other: Describe it below and I will take it into account.

priorities.speed: Go fast even if the boat heels and the sea turns uncomfortable.
priorities.comfort: Sail flat and steady rather than chase tenths of a knot.
priorities.racing: Racing: every adjustment counts, VMG and pointing rule.
priorities.safety: Margin before performance: reef early and keep heel low.
priorities.passage: Long passage: balance and little effort for the crew.
priorities.other: Tell me below what you care about.

zones.mediterranean: Thermal breezes, short sea and plenty of light summer air.
zones.atlantic: Long swell and shifting wind: trim for a built-up sea.
zones.caribbean: Steady trade winds and heat: consistent reaching breeze.
zones.pacific: Endless trades and long passages: prioritise durability.
zones.cantabrian: Strong wind and cross sea: reefing pays off.
zones.baltic: Light, puffy winds and little swell.
zones.north_sea: Cold, gusts and current: reef before you think you need to.
zones.indian_ocean: Powerful trades and long sea: demanding sailing.

timeOfDay.morning: Breeze still light: soft trim and sails with shape.
timeOfDay.midday: The thermal at its peak: the strongest wind of the day.
timeOfDay.afternoon: Breeze settled in and the sea picked up.
timeOfDay.night: Poor visibility: keep changes simple and safe.
